mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate compresses equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate financing costs fall.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines for two consecutive months (t-test p>0.05 vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A 5% month-over-month decline in housing starts signals deteriorating consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as recession risks rise.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered periods (HOUST decline >5% MoM).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate and unemployment rate indicate aggressive monetary tightening amid labor market weakness, causing negative equity returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (FEDFUNDS up and UNRATE up) fails to predict negative returns in more than 55% of cases (20-day returns positive >45% of the time).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle regimes, a 2% monthly decline in retail sales (RSAFS) signals collapsing consumer spending, driving negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days as recession approaches.
failure_condition: In late-cycle regimes (UNRATE < 4.5% and FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), RSAFS decline >2% MoM fails to predict negative 60-day returns in >55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong monthly job growth (PAYEMS > 150k) indicates robust labor market conditions, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months with PAYEMS growth >150k (t-test p>0.05 vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI inflation rate above 4.0% triggers hawkish monetary policy expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days as rate hikes accelerate.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signal broad economic contraction, driving negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (INDPRO down and HOUST down) fails to predict negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In post-shock recovery regimes, a rebound in industrial production (INDPRO > 1.0% MoM) signals strengthening supply chains, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: In post-shock recovery regimes (UNRATE > 5.0% and FEDFUNDS > 3.5% in prior quarter), INDPRO rebound >1.0% MoM fails to predict positive 20-day returns in >55% of cases.
